control_test.question: Do the parameters lv=shuf and plpRedirect=mhFallback on a served destination show that a submitted short link failed to resolve to the intended product?
control_test.method: A separate fetcher requested https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3 directly — a bare, known-correct URL with no short link and no redirect in its chain — and the response was recorded verbatim on 2026-11-17.
control_test.observed: Served at https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3?lv=shuf&channelId=500&plpRedirect=mhFallback with the register's recorded title.
control_test.implication: The marker is attached when a detail page is served to this fetcher whether or not a short link was involved, so it is not evidence about a submitted link. Twelve passes of flags (F10, F14, F15, F41) give it as part of the reason product identity is unconfirmed.
control_test.what_still_justifies_the_caveat: Two facts that do not depend on the marker: the submitted tokens are nine characters where an ASIN is ten, so a token names no product by itself; and no account holder has recorded what each link was meant to point at, which is the only thing that could confirm intent.
control_test.status: Published as a caution against over-reading the marker, not as a rewording of those four rows. SG-38 asks a second reader to repeat the control (Q-29) before the wording is rewritten.
